sn12.2:1.2: [the Exalted One said this]:—“I will teach you, Monks, I will analyze* the causal law.
sn12.2:1.3: Listen to it, give your minds thoroughly and I will speak.’
sn12.2:2.1: What, Monks, is the causal law ?
sn12.2:3.1: And what, Monks, is old age-and-death?
sn12.2:3.2: That which, of this and that being, in this and that group, is decay, decrepitude, breaking up, hoariness, wrinkling of the skin, shrinkage of a life-span, over-ripeness of faculties:
sn12.2:3.4: That which, of this and that being from this or that group, is falling or decease, separation, disappearance, mortality or dying,* accomplishment of time: separation of component factors,> laying down of the carcase:
sn12.2:3.6: Thus it is this decay and this dying
sn12.2:4.2: That which, of this and that being in this and that group, is birth, continuous birth, descent,® reproduction, appearance of component factors, acquiring of sense-spheres.
sn12.2:5.3: becoming in Kama-[worlds]’ becoming in Rupa-[worlds], becoming in Arupa-[worlds].
sn12.2:6.3: grasping of desires, grasping of opinion, grasping of rule and ritual, grasping of soul-theory.
sn12.2:7.2: There are these six groups of craving:
sn12.2:7.3: craving for things seen, for things heard, for odours, for tastes, for things tangible, for ideas.
sn12.2:8.2: There are these six groups of feeling:
sn12.2:8.3: feeling that is born of eye-contact, feeling that is born of ear-contact, feeling that is born of nose-contact, feeling that is born of tongue-contact, feeling that 1s born of body-contact, feeling that is born of mind-contact.
sn12.2:9.2: There are these six groups of contact:
sn12.2:9.3: eye-contact, ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, mind-contact.
sn12.2:10.1: And what, Monks, is sixfold sense?
sn12.2:10.2: The sense of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind
sn12.2:11.2: Feeling, perception, will, contact, work of mind.
sn12.2:11.4: The four great elements and the shape derived from them.
sn12.2:11.6: This is the name, this is the shape
sn12.2:12.2: These are the six groups of consciousness :
sn12.2:12.3: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, smell-, taste-, touch-, and mind-consciousness.
sn12.2:14.2: Nescience concerning ill, its rise, its cessation and concerning the way going to the cessation of ill.
sn12.2:15.1: So thus, Monks:—‘ conditioned by ignorance activities.'
sn12.2:15.2: conditioned by activities consciousness,’ and so on to 'despair'
sn12.2:15.3: —such is the uprising of this entire mass of ill.
sn12.2:15.4: But from the utter fading out and ceasing of ignorance, ceasing of activities,
sn12.2:15.5: from the ceasing of activities ceasing of consciousness,
sn12.2:15.6: such is the ceasing of this entire mass of ill.
